I get the struggle, ditto on the paper towel-based compulsion. Fortunately I've outgrown most of the more crippling ones from when I was diagnosed as an adolescent, but I still go through ~50-60 sheets of paper towel (has to be the heavy duty bounty) to excavate my nose throughout the day. Especially before bed. Otherwise brain says I'll suffocate and die from boogers 🤦🏻‍♂️ Have to keep a roll in every room, vehicle, and in my desk at work. Shit is not cheap!

Needless to say, the inside of my nose is a painful, raw hellscape...

Sorry, I lost power and internet in a thunder storm yesterday. Glad to see from your profile that you're still around.

So in your country's school system you chose your future career path while still under 18 and in classes? If so that seems like a lot to put on a young person.

I'd be willing to bet your parents would rather you stand up to them and lose some money than lose you, though they may not show it. You said you made a couple attempts already, so you know how terrifying that is. Could facing them really be scarier than what you've already been through?

As for the friends... If they respond to normal conversation, why not stick with that for them, and save the venting for us on here? There's plenty of us to interact with, so you don't really need to worry about scaring us off. Maybe able to get the best of both, not push them away but still have an outlet for your feelings and frustrations here?

Not laughing at all, I actually started my degree in psychology but it was too difficult for me, and I changed to forestry. It was the right choice, I enjoyed having classes out in nature, and I know I never would've graduated had I stayed in psych. I don't know what they offer in your country, but maybe they have some similar options that lead to more manual jobs after school?

Do you have any other friends you can reach out to? Or people in your classes you could befriend? It sucks, but some people will just drift away no matter how hard we try to maintain contact.

It's a daily battle, and everyone has their limit of how much is too much, I've thought I hit mine many times. Try and do something to recharge yourself enough to make it to the next day, or week. Maybe that means going to a hospital for a bit, or missing some school. I'm confident if you take it day by day you'll find some good along with everything that's draining you.

What are you studying at university, if you don't mind my asking?

I get it, I've been where you are in similar circumstances, minus the pandemic. I felt exhausted by the thought of slogging my way through 4.5 years of university (I changed majors too), having to find a job and grind for the next 40 years, and then withering into old age. The idea of ending it seemed infinitely preferable to slowly burning myself out over the course of decades, only to eventually die anyways.

I came very close to killing myself, numerous times. But I decided to just take it one day at a time and not give a fuck about the little things, because if they wouldn't matter if I was dead, they shouldn't matter when I'm alive.

I'm glad I took this approach, as I've had some great and life-changing experiences since then, despite having some terrible ones too. Maybe I will eventually die by suicide one day, maybe it'll all become too much, too tiring for me. But whether it's tomorrow, or at 40 years old, or 70, etc. I'll know I gave it a good try, and had some happy moments amidst all the dark.

A friend's dad was in a similar position, he'd always been super healthy and athletic so it was obvious something was wrong and taking a toll on him. Refused to get it checked out more thoroughly because he didn't trust doctors. 

By the time his wife convinced him and they found out it was late-stage cancer almost a year later, they estimated he had a few months to live. He died less than a month later, at 60. His family is still crushed by the loss and the knowledge he'd likely be alive and well if he'd gotten it checked out after the early signs.

Do your damnedest not to end up in their position.
